name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q01 - Extreme habitats inhabited by microbes

questiontext.text: Which of the following extreme habitats can support the presence of microbes even when no other life-form can exist there?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Microbes are ubiquitous components of biological systems and exhibit remarkable physiological adaptability to extreme environmental conditions.

Step 2: Evaluation
Microbes are present not only in soil, water, air, and inside plants and animals, but also deep inside thermal vents (geysers) at temperatures as high as \(100^\circ\text{C}\), deep in soil, under thick layers of snow, and in highly acidic environments.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
All of the listed extreme habitats—deep thermal vents, thick snow layers, and highly acidic environments—support microbial life.

answer.text: All of these: deep thermal vents up to 100°C, under thick snow layers, and highly acidic environments
Only neutral freshwater ponds at room temperature
Only the upper 5 cm of agricultural topsoil
Exclusively inside the tissues of macroscopic animals

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q02 - Nature of prions as infectious agents

questiontext.text: Among the diverse groups of microbes, prions are best described as:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Microbes encompass cellular organisms (protozoa, bacteria, fungi) as well as acellular infectious agents (viruses, viroids, and prions).

Step 2: Evaluation
Prions are specifically defined as proteinaceous infectious agents, lacking nucleic acid genomes unlike viruses and viroids.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Prions are proteinaceous infectious agents.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q03 - Microbial colonies on nutritive media

questiontext.text: Why are bacteria and many fungi grown on nutritive media in petri dishes during laboratory studies?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Individual bacterial and fungal cells are microscopic, making direct observation without magnification impossible.

Step 2: Evaluation
When grown on nutritive media, bacteria and many fungi multiply to form macroscopic colonies that can be seen with the naked eyes, which facilitates studies on micro-organisms.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
They form colonies visible to the naked eye, making them useful for microbial studies.

answer.text: To convert prokaryotic bacteria into multicellular eukaryotic fungi
To form colonies that can be seen with the naked eyes for studying micro-organisms
To eliminate the need for any nutrients during microbial growth

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q04 - Adenovirus and Tobacco Mosaic Virus characteristics

questiontext.text: Which of the following correctly pairs a virus with its characteristic disease or morphology?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Viruses exhibit distinct shapes (polyhedral, rod-shaped, or complex bacteriophage) and host specificities.

Step 2: Evaluation
Adenovirus causes respiratory infections in humans and has a polyhedral shape, whereas Tobacco Mosaic Virus (TMV) is a compact rod-shaped plant virus. Bacteriophages infect bacteria rather than causing respiratory infections in humans.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Adenovirus causes respiratory infections and Tobacco Mosaic Virus is rod-shaped.

answer.text: Tobacco Mosaic Virus — spherical virus with tail prongs
Adenovirus — causes respiratory infections; Tobacco Mosaic Virus — rod-shaped

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q05 - Incorrect statement about microbial diversity

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements regarding microbes is incorrect?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Microbes include both harmful pathogens and numerous beneficial organisms that play vital roles in human welfare.

Step 2: Evaluation
1. Microbes are diverse and include protozoa, bacteria, fungi, viruses, viroids, and prions.
2. Many microbes can survive in extreme environments such as thermal vents up to \(100^\circ\text{C}\).
3. Although many microbes cause diseases in humans, animals, and plants, several microbes are useful to humans in diverse ways—so claiming that all microbes are pathogenic is false.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The statement that all microbes are pathogenic and harmful to human beings is incorrect.

answer.text: All microbes are pathogenic and harmful to human beings, animals, and plants.
Microbes include protozoa, bacteria, fungi, viruses, viroids, and prions.
Bacteria and many fungi can be grown on nutritive media to form visible colonies.
Microbes can survive inside geysers where temperatures may reach 100°C.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q06 - Action of lactic acid bacteria on milk proteins

questiontext.text: During the conversion of milk into curd, lactic acid bacteria (LAB) produce acids that:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Lactic acid bacteria (such as Lactobacillus) ferment lactose in milk and release organic acids.

Step 2: Evaluation
The acids produced by LAB during growth coagulate and partially digest the milk proteins, transforming liquid milk into curd.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
LAB produce acids that coagulate and partially digest milk proteins.

answer.text: Convert milk fats into ethanol and carbon dioxide
Coagulate and partially digest the milk proteins
Completely destroy all vitamins present in milk

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q07 - Vitamin increased in curd by LAB

questiontext.text: Conversion of milk to curd by lactic acid bacteria improves its nutritional quality primarily by increasing the content of:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Fermentation of milk by lactic acid bacteria (LAB) enhances both digestibility and micronutrient content.

Step 2: Evaluation
As LAB multiply in milk and convert it to curd, they improve its nutritional quality by increasing vitamin \(\text{B}_{12}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Vitamin \(\text{B}_{12}\) content increases during curd formation.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q08 - Beneficial role of LAB in human stomach

questiontext.text: Apart from converting milk into curd, what beneficial role do lactic acid bacteria (LAB) play inside the human stomach?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Beneficial gut and gastric microbes help maintain host health through microbial antagonism.

Step 2: Evaluation
In the human stomach, LAB play a very beneficial role in checking disease-causing microbes. They do not fix atmospheric nitrogen, digest cellulose, or secrete insulin.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
LAB check disease-causing microbes in the stomach.

answer.text: They fix atmospheric nitrogen into amino acids
They secrete pectinases to clarify ingested fruit juices

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q09 - Cause of puffed-up appearance in dosa and idli dough

questiontext.text: The puffed-up appearance of dough used for making dosa and idli is due to the production of:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Fermentation of carbohydrate-rich dough by bacteria releases gaseous metabolic by-products.

Step 2: Evaluation
The dough used for making dosa and idli is fermented by bacteria, and the trapped \(\text{CO}_2\) gas produced during fermentation causes the dough to puff up.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The puffed-up appearance is due to \(\text{CO}_2\) gas.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q10 - Baker's yeast in bread making

questiontext.text: Which micro-organism is commonly known as baker's yeast and used for fermenting dough to make bread?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Yeasts are unicellular fungi widely used in baking and brewing industries.

Step 2: Evaluation
The dough used for making bread is fermented using baker's yeast, which is Saccharomyces cerevisiae.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Saccharomyces cerevisiae is baker's yeast.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q11 - Preparation of traditional drink Toddy

questiontext.text: 'Toddy', a traditional drink of some parts of southern India, is prepared by fermenting:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Traditional fermented beverages and foods are prepared locally using naturally occurring microbes on plant substrates.

Step 2: Evaluation
'Toddy' is made by fermenting sap from palms. Other substrates like soyabean, fish, and bamboo-shoots are fermented to make traditional foods, not toddy.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Toddy is made by fermenting sap from palms.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q12 - Bacterium responsible for large holes in Swiss cheese

questiontext.text: The large holes in 'Swiss cheese' are formed due to the production of a large amount of CO2 by:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Different varieties of cheese owe their characteristic texture, flavour, and taste to the specific microbes used during ripening.

Step 2: Evaluation
The large holes in Swiss cheese are caused by large amounts of \(\text{CO}_2\) produced by the bacterium Propionibacterium sharmanii.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Propionibacterium sharmanii produces the \(\text{CO}_2\) responsible for the holes in Swiss cheese.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q13 - Microbial specificity in Swiss and Roquefort cheese

questiontext.text: Which of the following correctly differentiates the ripening agents of Swiss cheese and Roquefort cheese?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cheese varieties acquire their distinctive texture and flavour from specific bacterial or fungal cultures.

Step 2: Evaluation
Swiss cheese is produced using a bacterium (Propionibacterium sharmanii), whereas Roquefort cheese is ripened by growing a specific fungus on it, which imparts its particular flavour.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Swiss cheese uses a bacterium and Roquefort cheese is ripened using specific fungi.

answer.text: Swiss cheese uses a bacterium, whereas Roquefort cheese is ripened by growing specific fungi
Swiss cheese uses a fungus, whereas Roquefort cheese is ripened by a bacterium
Both Swiss cheese and Roquefort cheese are ripened exclusively by Saccharomyces cerevisiae
Both Swiss cheese and Roquefort cheese are ripened exclusively by cyanobacteria

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q14 - Large vessels used for industrial microbial production

questiontext.text: Production of beverages and antibiotics on an industrial scale requires growing microbes in very large vessels called:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Industrial microbiology requires controlled, large-volume vessels to culture micro-organisms at commercial scale.

Step 2: Evaluation
Large vessels used to grow microbes on an industrial scale for synthesising beverages, antibiotics, and other products are called fermentors.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The large vessels are called fermentors.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q15 - Brewer's yeast fermentation of cereals and fruit juices

questiontext.text: Brewer's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) is used in the beverage industry to ferment malted cereals and fruit juices to produce:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Alcoholic fermentation by yeast converts sugars present in malted cereals and fruit juices into alcohol.

Step 2: Evaluation
Saccharomyces cerevisiae (brewer's yeast) ferments malted cereals and fruit juices to produce ethanol.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The primary alcoholic product formed is ethanol.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q16 - Alcoholic beverages produced with distillation

questiontext.text: Which of the following groups of alcoholic drinks is produced by distillation of the fermented broth?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The type of alcoholic beverage obtained depends on both the raw material fermented and whether the fermented broth undergoes distillation.

Step 2: Evaluation
Wine and beer are produced without distillation, whereas whisky, brandy, and rum are produced by distillation of the fermented broth.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Whisky, brandy, and rum are produced by distillation.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q17 - Factors determining types of alcoholic drinks

questiontext.text: Despite using the same yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae, different types of alcoholic drinks are obtained in industry depending on:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Saccharomyces cerevisiae produces ethanol from sugars, but the final beverage category varies widely.

Step 2: Evaluation
The variety of alcoholic drinks (such as wine, beer, whisky, brandy, or rum) depends on two main factors: the type of raw material used for fermentation (e.g., malted cereals or fruit juices) and the type of processing (with or without distillation).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both the raw material used for fermentation and whether distillation is performed determine the type of alcoholic drink obtained.

answer.text: The type of raw material used for fermentation and whether processing involves distillation
The addition of Propionibacterium sharmanii to the fermented broth
Whether the fermentation is carried out in petri dishes or anaerobic sludge digesters
The replacement of ethanol production with lactic acid production

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q18 - Etymology and meaning of antibiotics

questiontext.text: In the context of human welfare, antibiotics are described as 'against life' with respect to disease-causing organisms, whereas with reference to human beings they are:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The Greek roots anti ('against') and bio ('life') together mean 'against life'.

Step 2: Evaluation
Antibiotics are 'against life' in the context of disease-causing microbes because they kill or retard their growth; however, with reference to human beings, they are 'pro life' and not against.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
With reference to human beings, antibiotics are 'pro life'.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q19 - Bacterium studied by Alexander Fleming during penicillin discovery

questiontext.text: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin by chance while working on which bacterium in his culture plates?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Penicillin was the first antibiotic discovered, arising from an accidental observation of microbial antagonism on a culture plate.

Step 2: Evaluation
While working on Staphylococci bacteria, Alexander Fleming observed a mould (Penicillium notatum) growing on an unwashed culture plate around which Staphylococci could not grow.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Fleming was working on Staphylococci bacteria.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q20 - Chain and Florey establishing full potential of penicillin

questiontext.text: The full potential of penicillin as an effective antibiotic was established much later than its initial discovery by:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Translating a laboratory discovery into a clinically effective therapeutic agent often requires subsequent purification and efficacy testing.

Step 2: Evaluation
Although Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin, its full potential as an effective antibiotic was established much later by Ernest Chain and Howard Florey. It was extensively used to treat wounded American soldiers in World War II, and Fleming, Chain, and Florey shared the 1945 Nobel Prize.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Ernest Chain and Howard Florey established the full potential of penicillin.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q21 - Deadly bacterial diseases treated using antibiotics

questiontext.text: Antibiotics have greatly improved our capacity to treat deadly diseases such as:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Antibiotics target bacterial pathogens and have drastically reduced mortality from severe infectious diseases.

Step 2: Evaluation
Antibiotics have greatly improved the treatment of deadly diseases such as plague, whooping cough (kali khansi), diphtheria (gal ghotu), and leprosy (kusht rog). Myocardial infarction and high blood cholesterol are non-infectious cardiovascular conditions.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Plague, whooping cough, diphtheria, and leprosy are treated using antibiotics.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q22 - Incorrect statement about Penicillin history

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements about the antibiotic penicillin is incorrect?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The history of penicillin involves its chance discovery, subsequent clinical development, and military application during World War II.

Step 2: Evaluation
1. Penicillin was the first antibiotic discovered and was named after the mould Penicillium notatum.
2. It was extensively used to treat wounded American soldiers in World War II.
3. Fleming, Chain, and Florey were awarded the Nobel Prize in 1945.
4. Penicillin is produced by a mould (fungus), not a bacterium.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The statement that penicillin was isolated from a bacterium is incorrect.

answer.text: It was extensively used to treat American soldiers wounded in World War II.
It was isolated from a bacterium named Penicillium notatum.
Fleming, Chain, and Florey were awarded the Nobel Prize in 1945 for this discovery.
It was the first antibiotic to be discovered and was a chance discovery.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q23 - Commercial producer of citric acid

questiontext.text: Which of the following microbes is used for the commercial production of citric acid?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Specific fungi and bacteria are cultured industrially to produce organic acids.

Step 2: Evaluation
Aspergillus niger (a fungus) is the commercial producer of citric acid. Acetobacter aceti produces acetic acid, Clostridium butylicum produces butyric acid, and Lactobacillus produces lactic acid.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Aspergillus niger is used for commercial production of citric acid.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q24 - Bacterial vs fungal organic acid producers

questiontext.text: Which of the following pairs consists exclusively of bacterial producers of organic acids?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Industrial organic acid producers belong to either fungi (e.g., Aspergillus niger) or bacteria.

Step 2: Evaluation
Acetobacter aceti (acetic acid), Clostridium butylicum (butyric acid), and Lactobacillus (lactic acid) are all bacteria. By contrast, Aspergillus niger (citric acid) is a fungus and Saccharomyces cerevisiae is a yeast (fungus) used for ethanol production.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Acetobacter aceti, Clostridium butylicum, and Lactobacillus are exclusively bacterial organic acid producers.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q25 - Role of lipases in detergent formulations

questiontext.text: Which microbial enzymes are added to detergent formulations to help remove oily stains from laundry?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Enzymes catalyse the breakdown of specific macromolecules; oily stains consist of lipids (fats and oils).

Step 2: Evaluation
Lipases break down lipids and are therefore used in detergent formulations to remove oily stains from laundry. Pectinases and proteases clarify bottled fruit juices, while streptokinase acts as a clot buster.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Lipases are used in detergent formulations for removing oily stains.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q26 - Enzymes clarifying bottled fruit juices

questiontext.text: Bottled fruit juices bought from the market appear clearer than homemade fruit juices because they are clarified using:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cloudiness in extracted fruit juices is caused by suspended pectin and protein particles.

Step 2: Evaluation
Commercial bottled fruit juices are clarified using pectinases and proteases, which break down pectin and proteins to yield a clear liquid.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Pectinases and proteases are used to clarify bottled fruit juices.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q27 - Streptokinase as clot buster

questiontext.text: Which enzyme, produced by Streptococcus and modified by genetic engineering, is used as a 'clot buster' in patients who have undergone myocardial infarction?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Myocardial infarction (heart attack) is caused by blood clots blocking coronary blood vessels; dissolving these clots restores blood flow.

Step 2: Evaluation
Streptokinase, produced by the bacterium Streptococcus and modified by genetic engineering, is used as a 'clot buster' to remove clots from the blood vessels of patients who have undergone myocardial infarction.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Streptokinase is used as a clot buster.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q28 - Cyclosporin A source and clinical use

questiontext.text: An organ-transplant patient is prescribed an immunosuppressive drug obtained from a fungus. Identify the drug and its source organism.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Organ-transplant patients require immunosuppressive agents to prevent immune rejection of the transplanted organ.

Step 2: Evaluation
Cyclosporin A is used as an immunosuppressive agent in organ-transplant patients, and it is produced by the fungus Trichoderma polysporum. Statins from Monascus purpureus lower blood cholesterol, while streptokinase from Streptococcus dissolves blood clots.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The drug is cyclosporin A, obtained from Trichoderma polysporum.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q29 - Mechanism of action of statins

questiontext.text: Statins produced by the yeast Monascus purpureus lower blood cholesterol levels by:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Enzyme inhibitors can regulate metabolic pathways such as endogenous cholesterol biosynthesis.

Step 2: Evaluation
Statins act as blood-cholesterol lowering agents by competitively inhibiting the enzyme responsible for the synthesis of cholesterol.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Statins act by competitively inhibiting the enzyme responsible for cholesterol synthesis.

answer.text: Competitively inhibiting the enzyme responsible for cholesterol synthesis
Directly hydrolysing cholesterol in blood plasma using lipases
Suppressing the host immune system during organ transplantation

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q30 - Incorrect pairing of bioactive molecule and microbe

questiontext.text: Which of the following combinations of bioactive molecule, source organism, and its microbial group is incorrect?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Accurate classification of industrial microbes (fungi, yeasts, and bacteria) is essential for linking bioactive products to their biological sources.

Step 2: Evaluation
1. Cyclosporin A is produced by Trichoderma polysporum, which is a fungus.
2. Statins are produced by Monascus purpureus, which is a yeast.
3. Citric acid is produced by Aspergillus niger, which is a fungus.
4. Streptokinase is produced by Streptococcus, which is a bacterium, not a fungus.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The pairing describing streptokinase from Streptococcus as a fungus is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q31 - Physical processes in primary sewage treatment

questiontext.text: Primary treatment of municipal sewage basically involves the physical removal of large and small particles through:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Sewage treatment begins with physical separation before biological oxidation.

Step 2: Evaluation
Primary treatment steps involve physical removal of particles through sequential filtration (to remove floating debris) and sedimentation (to remove grit such as soil and small pebbles).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Primary treatment relies on filtration and sedimentation.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q32 - Primary sludge vs effluent in sewage treatment

questiontext.text: In the primary settling tank of a sewage treatment plant, what happens to the settled solids and the supernatant?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Sedimentation in the primary settling tank separates denser solids from the overlying liquid.

Step 2: Evaluation
All solids that settle form the primary sludge, while the supernatant forms the effluent, which is taken for secondary (biological) treatment.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Settled solids form primary sludge, and the supernatant forms the effluent sent for secondary treatment.

answer.text: Settled solids form activated sludge and the supernatant is discharged directly into rivers
Settled solids form the effluent and the supernatant forms primary sludge
Both settled solids and supernatant are pumped into anaerobic sludge digesters
Settled solids form primary sludge and the supernatant forms the effluent taken for secondary treatment

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q33 - Composition of flocs in aeration tanks

questiontext.text: In the aeration tanks of secondary sewage treatment, 'flocs' are best defined as:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Mechanical agitation and air pumping in aeration tanks promote vigorous growth of useful aerobic heterotrophic microbes.

Step 2: Evaluation
These aerobic microbes grow into flocs, which are masses of bacteria associated with fungal filaments to form mesh-like structures.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Flocs are mesh-like structures formed by masses of aerobic bacteria associated with fungal filaments.

answer.text: Masses of aerobic bacteria associated with fungal filaments to form mesh-like structures
Inorganic grit, soil, and pebbles removed during primary sedimentation
Colonies of anaerobic methanogens growing in sealed concrete tanks

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q34 - Meaning and significance of BOD

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements accurately describes Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
BOD is a standard water-quality parameter used to assess organic pollution in sewage and natural water bodies.

Step 2: Evaluation
BOD refers to the amount of oxygen that would be consumed if all the organic matter in one litre of water were oxidised by bacteria. By measuring the rate of oxygen uptake by micro-organisms, BOD serves as an indirect measure of organic matter present: the greater the BOD of waste water, the more is its polluting potential.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
BOD is the oxygen consumed when all organic matter in one litre of water is oxidised by bacteria, and higher BOD indicates greater polluting potential.

answer.text: It is the amount of oxygen released by photosynthetic cyanobacteria in one litre of sewage.
It is the amount of oxygen consumed if all organic matter in one litre of water were oxidised by bacteria; higher BOD means greater polluting potential.
It measures the concentration of inorganic grit in primary sludge; higher BOD means cleaner water.
It is the volume of methane produced per litre of water in anaerobic sludge digesters.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q35 - Role of recycled activated sludge as inoculum

questiontext.text: Why is a small part of the activated sludge pumped back into the aeration tank during secondary sewage treatment?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Continuous secondary treatment requires a steady population of aerobic floc-forming microbes in the aeration tank.

Step 2: Evaluation
After BOD is reduced and bacterial flocs sediment as activated sludge in the settling tank, a small portion of this activated sludge is pumped back into the aeration tank to serve as the inoculum for incoming primary effluent.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
It is pumped back to serve as the inoculum.

answer.text: To supply anaerobic methanogens to the aeration tank
To increase the grit and floating debris content
To serve as the inoculum of aerobic microbes
To raise the BOD of the treated effluent before river discharge

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q36 - Gases produced in anaerobic sludge digesters

questiontext.text: In anaerobic sludge digesters, anaerobic bacteria digest the bacteria and fungi in the activated sludge to produce a mixture of gases forming biogas. This gas mixture consists of:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The major part of activated sludge is pumped into anaerobic sludge digesters for breakdown in the absence of oxygen.

Step 2: Evaluation
During anaerobic digestion of the bacteria and fungi in the sludge, anaerobic bacteria produce a mixture of gases—methane (\(\text{CH}_4\)), hydrogen sulphide (\(\text{H}_2\text{S}\)), and carbon dioxide (\(\text{CO}_2\))—which form inflammable biogas.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The biogas mixture formed in anaerobic sludge digesters consists of methane, hydrogen sulphide, and carbon dioxide.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q37 - Ganga Action Plan and Yamuna Action Plan

questiontext.text: The Ganga Action Plan and Yamuna Action Plan were initiated by the Ministry of Environment and Forests primarily to:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Increasing urbanisation generates more sewage than existing treatment plants can handle, leading to direct discharge into rivers and water-borne diseases.

Step 2: Evaluation
Under the Ganga Action Plan and Yamuna Action Plan, it is proposed to build a large number of sewage treatment plants so that only treated sewage is discharged into these major rivers, saving them from pollution.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The plans aim to build more sewage treatment plants so only treated sewage is discharged into the rivers.

answer.text: Build a large number of sewage treatment plants so only treated sewage is discharged into the rivers
Introduce chemical pesticides along riverbanks to eliminate aquatic microbes
Increase the BOD of river water by adding untreated municipal waste
Replace microbial sewage treatment with purely synthetic chemical oxidation

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q38 - Gases produced by methanogens on cellulosic material

questiontext.text: Methanogens such as Methanobacterium grow anaerobically on cellulosic material to produce large amounts of:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The type of gas produced by microbes during metabolism depends on the microbe and the organic substrate utilised.

Step 2: Evaluation
Bacteria called methanogens (e.g., Methanobacterium) grow anaerobically on cellulosic material and produce large amounts of methane along with \(\text{CO}_2\) and \(\text{H}_2\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
They produce methane along with \(\text{CO}_2\) and \(\text{H}_2\).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q39 - Methanogens in the rumen of cattle

questiontext.text: In the rumen of cattle, methanogenic bacteria play an important role in cattle nutrition by:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cattle feed contains a large amount of cellulosic plant material, which requires microbial enzymes for digestion.

Step 2: Evaluation
Methanogens present in the rumen (a part of the stomach) of cattle help in the breakdown of cellulose, playing a vital role in cattle nutrition and making cattle dung (gobar) rich in these bacteria.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Methanogens help in the breakdown of cellulose in the rumen of cattle.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q40 - Use of spent slurry from a biogas plant

questiontext.text: In a typical biogas plant, the spent slurry removed through the secondary outlet is commonly used as:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A biogas plant converts bio-wastes and cattle dung slurry into two useful outputs: gaseous fuel and nutrient-rich residue.

Step 2: Evaluation
While the biogas collected under the rising floating cover is piped to nearby houses for cooking and lighting, the spent slurry removed through another outlet is used as fertiliser.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The spent slurry is used as fertiliser.

answer.text: A detergent additive for removing oily stains

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q41 - Biogas technology institutions and gaseous comparison

questiontext.text: In India, the technology of biogas production was developed mainly through the efforts of:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Rural biogas plants rely on cattle dung (gobar) and standardised engineering designs developed by Indian agricultural and village-industry institutions.

Step 2: Evaluation
Biogas production technology in India was developed mainly due to the efforts of the Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) and the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
IARI and KVIC developed biogas production technology in India.

answer.text: Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) and Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)
Ministry of Environment and Forests under the Ganga Action Plan
World Health Organization and Food Safety Authority
National Dairy Development Board and Indian Medical Council

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q42 - Organic farming approach to pest control

questiontext.text: Why does an organic farmer consider the complete eradication of pests undesirable?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Organic farming is a holistic approach based on the belief that biodiversity furthers health and sustainability.

Step 2: Evaluation
Rather than eradicating pests completely, organic farmers keep them at manageable levels through checks and balances, because without pests, the beneficial predatory and parasitic insects that depend on them as food or hosts would not be able to survive.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Without pests, beneficial predatory and parasitic insects that depend on them for food or as hosts would not survive.

answer.text: Because pests are required to fix atmospheric nitrogen in paddy fields
Because beneficial predatory and parasitic insects depending on pests as food or hosts would not survive
Because chemical insecticides cannot be manufactured without live pests
Because pests directly produce mycorrhizal associations with crop roots

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q43 - Ladybird beetles and dragonflies in biocontrol

questiontext.text: Ladybird beetles and dragonflies are useful biological control agents to get rid of which pests, respectively?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Natural predators in agricultural and surrounding ecosystems help control specific insect pests without chemical pesticides.

Step 2: Evaluation
The beetle with red and black markings—the Ladybird—is useful to get rid of aphids, while dragonflies are useful to get rid of mosquitoes.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Ladybird beetles control aphids and dragonflies control mosquitoes.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q44 - Bacillus thuringiensis and Bt-cotton

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements about Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) as a biocontrol agent is correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Bacillus thuringiensis is a bacterium whose spores and toxin genes are used both as sprayed microbial formulations and in genetically engineered crops.

Step 2: Evaluation
Dried Bt spores are mixed with water and sprayed onto vulnerable plants like brassicas and fruit trees; when ingested by butterfly caterpillars, the toxin is released in the larval gut and kills the caterpillars while leaving other insects unharmed. Scientists have also introduced B. thuringiensis toxin genes into plants such as Bt-cotton to confer pest resistance.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The toxin is released in the larval gut upon ingestion, killing caterpillars while leaving non-target insects unharmed, and its toxin genes have been introduced into Bt-cotton.

answer.text: It is a fungus that kills both caterpillars and beneficial ladybird beetles indiscriminately.
Its dried spores kill plants such as brassicas and fruit trees upon contact.
It is a baculovirus that infects mammals and birds in ecologically sensitive areas.
Its toxin is released in the gut of larvae to kill caterpillars while leaving other insects unharmed, and its toxin genes are used in Bt-cotton.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q45 - Trichoderma and Nucleopolyhedrovirus in biocontrol

questiontext.text: Which of the following correctly describes Trichoderma and Nucleopolyhedrovirus in biological control?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Microbial biocontrol agents include free-living root-associated fungi as well as species-specific insect viruses.

Step 2: Evaluation
Trichoderma species are free-living fungi common in root ecosystems that act as effective biocontrol agents of several plant pathogens. Nucleopolyhedrovirus belongs to baculoviruses and provides species-specific, narrow-spectrum insecticidal applications with no negative impacts on plants, mammals, birds, fish, or non-target insects—making it desirable in integrated pest management (IPM).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Trichoderma is a free-living root-ecosystem fungus against plant pathogens, while Nucleopolyhedrovirus is a narrow-spectrum baculovirus ideal for IPM.

answer.text: Trichoderma is a free-living root-ecosystem fungus effective against plant pathogens; Nucleopolyhedrovirus is a narrow-spectrum baculovirus ideal for IPM
Trichoderma is a nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterium; Nucleopolyhedrovirus is a broad-spectrum chemical weedicide
Both Trichoderma and Nucleopolyhedrovirus are methanogenic bacteria found in cattle rumen
Trichoderma produces statins; Nucleopolyhedrovirus is used to ferment palm sap into toddy

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q46 - Free-living nitrogen-fixing bacteria in soil

questiontext.text: Unlike Rhizobium, which forms symbiotic root nodules in leguminous plants, which of the following bacteria can fix atmospheric nitrogen while free-living in the soil?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Nitrogen-fixing bacterial biofertilisers include both symbiotic root-nodule bacteria and free-living soil bacteria.

Step 2: Evaluation
Azospirillum and Azotobacter fix atmospheric nitrogen while free-living in the soil, thereby enriching the nitrogen content of the soil.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Azospirillum and Azotobacter are free-living nitrogen-fixing bacteria.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q47 - Benefits of Glomus mycorrhizal association to plants

questiontext.text: Plants forming mycorrhizal associations with fungi of the genus Glomus derive which of the following sets of benefits?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Mycorrhiza is a symbiotic association between fungi (many belonging to the genus Glomus) and plant roots.

Step 2: Evaluation
In mycorrhizal associations, the fungal symbiont absorbs phosphorus from the soil and passes it to the plant. Plants with mycorrhiza also exhibit resistance to root-borne pathogens, tolerance to salinity and drought, and an overall increase in plant growth and development.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The plant receives phosphorus from soil, resistance to root-borne pathogens, and tolerance to salinity and drought.

answer.text: Direct conversion of milk proteins and increased vitamin B12
Production of methane gas and reduction of sewage BOD
Phosphorus absorption from soil, resistance to root-borne pathogens, and tolerance to salinity and drought
Release of Bt toxin in the gut of caterpillars and viral immunity

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBESINHUMANWELFARE_MCQ_Q48 - Cyanobacteria as biofertilisers in paddy fields

questiontext.text: Which group of autotrophic microbes—including Anabaena, Nostoc, and Oscillatoria—serves as an important biofertiliser in paddy fields by fixing atmospheric nitrogen and adding organic matter to the soil?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Biofertilisers enrich soil nutrient quality using bacteria, fungi, and autotrophic blue-green algae.

Step 2: Evaluation
Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) such as Anabaena, Nostoc, and Oscillatoria are autotrophic microbes widely distributed in aquatic and terrestrial environments. Many of them fix atmospheric nitrogen, serve as important biofertilisers in paddy fields, and add organic matter to the soil to increase fertility.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) perform these roles in paddy fields.
